title: Boundary-Scan Register (4 Cells)
constraints: Four IEEE 1149.1 BC_1-style cells. Each has a **capture/shift** flop `cap[i]` and an **update** flop `upd[i]`. All flops are clocked by `clk`, and at most one of capture/shift/update is active per edge.
`capture_dr`: `cap <= data_in`. `shift_dr`: the chain shifts, with `cap[0] <= scan_in`, `cap[i] <= cap[i-1]`, and `scan_out = cap[3]` (combinational). `update_dr`: `upd <= cap`.
`data_out[i] = mode ? upd[i] : data_in[i]`: normal mode passes the pins through, and test mode (EXTEST) drives the updated values. Synchronous reset clears both registers.
hints: The update register exists so that the pins don't ripple while new values are being shifted in.
`cap` is just a loadable shift register. `upd` is a parallel register loaded from it.
In a real device these enables come from the TAP controller states Capture-DR, Shift-DR and Update-DR (see the JTAG TAP problem).
